rationale: Comprehensive phenotypic analysis across multiple cohorts of individuals with pathogenic KDM2B variants (including the seminal delineation by van Jaarsveld et al., the CxxC-specific cohort by van Oirsouw et al., and the large combined series by van Oirsouw et al.) confirms that affected individuals present with subtle or mild facial dysmorphism, developmental delay/intellectual disability, and structural malformations predominantly of the heart, eyes, and urogenital tract. Across all published cohorts (totaling over 47 confirmed pathogenic cases), severe limb reduction defects, ectrodactyly, and coarse lysosomal storage-like facial features have not been observed. Their presence strongly points toward alternative diagnoses (e.g., EEC syndrome, split-hand/foot malformation disorders, or lysosomal storage disorders) rather than KDM2B-related disorder.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 21 individuals with heterozygous pathogenic KDM2B variants, individuals exhibited developmental delay, intellectual disability, congenital organ anomalies (predominantly cardiac, ocular, and urogenital), and subtle facial dysmorphism, with no reported severe limb reduction defects, ectrodactyly, or coarse features.

source.title: Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated DNA methylation signature
source.quote: Individuals in this cohort present with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability; autism; attention deficit disorder/attention deficit hyperactivity disorder; congenital organ anomalies mainly of the heart, eyes, and urogenital system; and subtle facial dysmorphism.

evidence.text: In an expanded study evaluating 19 individuals with KDM2B CxxC domain variants, phenotypes centered on speech and motor delay, variable intellectual disability, mild facial dysmorphism, congenital heart defects (up to 78%), and musculoskeletal, ophthalmological, and urogenital anomalies, without any severe limb reduction anomalies or storage disease features.

source.title: KDM2B variants in the CxxC domain impair its DNA-binding ability and cause a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: All individuals with CxxC variants presented with developmental delay, mainly in the speech and motor domain, in addition to variable intellectual disability and mild facial dysmorphism. Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of individuals, with additional common findings including musculoskeletal, ophthalmological, and urogenital anomalies

evidence.text: A comprehensive assessment evaluating 68 individuals (with 47 confirmed pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants) observed a penetrant CxxC-related phenotype with distinct facial gestalt supported by GestaltMatcher, characterized by variable expressivity of LoF variants and lack of coarse lysosomal or ectrodactyly phenotypes.

source.title: Comprehensive Assessment of the KDM2B‐Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder and the 12q24. 31 Microdeletion Syndrome
source.quote: We analyzed genotype-phenotype correlations of this cohort combined with previously reported individuals (n = 68) and classify 37 variants in 47 individuals as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. We observe a highly penetrant CxxC-related phenotype with distinct facial features supported by GestaltMatcher.

evidence.text: Detailed clinical descriptions of three patients with KDM2B CxxC variants identified cardiac defects, feeding difficulties, solitary kidney, hip dysplasia, hemangiomas, hypertrichosis, and myopic astigmatism, with no severe reduction defects or coarse storage facies.

source.title: KDM2B‐Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder A Case‐Series Supporting the CxxC Domain Phenotype With Emphasis on Ocular and Dermatologic Features
source.quote: Patient 1 is a 2-year-old boy with developmental delay, solitary kidney, atrial septal defect, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 2 is a 2-year-old girl with global developmental delay, hip dysplasia, feeding difficulties, hemangiomas, and myopic astigmatism. Patient 3 is a 5-year-old girl with autism, developmental delay, atrial septal defect, and ventricular septal defect, hypertrichosis, atopic dermatitis, and myopic astigmatism.

new_directions.question_text: What specific minor distal limb or skeletal features (e.g., brachydactyly, clinodactyly, hip dysplasia) occur at measurable frequencies in KDM2B cohorts?
new_directions.rationale: While severe limb reductions and ectrodactyly are absent, minor musculoskeletal findings such as hip dysplasia have been described and warrant systematic cataloging across cohorts.

new_directions.question_text: Can automated computer-vision facial analysis tools (e.g., GestaltMatcher, Face2Gene) reliably differentiate KDM2B CxxC-domain mild dysmorphism from overlapping chromatinopathies such as KDM6B-related disorder?
new_directions.rationale: Given that dysmorphism in KDM2B is mild/subtle rather than coarse, quantitative facial analysis could enhance specificity when differentiating overlapping neurodevelopmental syndromes.
